# A stale e2e duration table lets engine shards drift to the ceiling

## Context

Two engine e2e shards hit the five-minute step ceiling today on pull requests whose tests all passed:

- neo `#21239` @ `098b335ee4`, `e2e-engine (13/14)`: "75 passed (5.1m)", then "The action 'Run e2e (engine tier)' has timed out after 5 minutes" (run 44040385390, defect note `73f2ec59`).
- outside PR `#21240` @ `280f5f6`, `e2e-engine (4/14)`: "63 passed (5.0m)", then the same timeout (run 44082682665). None of that PR's specs run in that shard. The contributor cannot re-run jobs and had to ask on the PR (https://github.com/neomjs/neo/pull/21240#issuecomment-6948763797).

Each occurrence costs a maintainer re-run. An outside contributor who cannot re-run waits on a red check their change did not cause.

## The Problem

`balancedShard()` splits the tier by measured seconds per spec file. The table it reads has fallen behind the tier:

- `buildScripts/util/e2eEngineDurations.json` lists 194 files. The tier (`enginePaths()`) has 223. The 29 missing files are mostly specs added since the last full rebuild (board, gantt, timeline, `core/ContentSecurityPolicy`, `grid/CountriesExample`, …), and each counts as the table's median.
- On dev's latest full run (44081473449 @ `d49f1dd494`, all green), the 14 shards' test steps took 195–236 s. Re-measured with that run's per-file times, the current split spreads from 189 to 230 s, while the table predicts at most 216 s.
- Over the last 45 completed pull-request runs (379 shard steps): p50 216 s, p90 256 s, p99 293 s, max 301 s. 19 steps took 270 s or more. The tail sits on top of the imbalance, so the heaviest shard is the one that times out.

## The Architectural Reality

- `.github/workflows/test-e2e.yml` header: "the ceiling is five minutes of test time per shard … A shard nearing it gets a sibling, never a higher ceiling". The step's `timeout-minutes` is 5 on `pull_request` and `push`.
- `buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs`: `FULL_SHARDS = {engine: 14}`, and `ENGINE_DURATIONS` is read from `e2eEngineDurations.json`. `balancedShard({paths, shard, durations})` assigns files by those seconds, and `--engine-durations` rebuilds the table from a full dev run's log (`gh run view <id> --log`).
- #20521 replaced count-based splitting with this table. Its Avoided Traps rule out "another shard" as a fix for an unbalanced split.

## The Fix

Regenerate `e2eEngineDurations.json` with the existing CLI from dev's latest full run: `gh run view 44081473449 --log | node buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs --engine-durations`. A full, green dev run is the only valid input. Measured before filing, with that run's log: the rebuilt table covers all 223 files, and the 14 shards predict 209–210 s each, against 189–230 s for the current split. The heaviest shard drops by about 20 s, roughly what a fifteenth shard would buy, without the extra runner. `FULL_SHARDS` and the ceiling stay.

Decision Record impact: none.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `e2eEngineDurations.json` holds a time for every `enginePaths()` file, rebuilt from a named full green dev run.
- [ ] The PR states each shard's predicted seconds with the old table and the new one. The new spread is at most 5 s.
- [ ] `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/E2eCiSelection.spec.mjs` passes.
- [ ] Post-merge: the next 20 pull-request runs show no engine shard step at the 300 s ceiling with all tests passed. A miss reopens the choice between a fifteenth shard and a refresh that runs by itself.

## Out of Scope

- Refreshing the table automatically in CI, as in #20521. 29 files went missing in about 8 days, so this ticket's post-merge AC measures whether a manual refresh is enough.
- The ceiling and `FULL_SHARDS.engine`.
- The `e2e-brain` tier's table.

## Avoided Traps

- **A fifteenth shard first.** It buys the same 20 s for one more runner on every pull request, and the split stays as unbalanced as the table is stale (#20521).
- **Raising the ceiling.** The header rules it out: the ceiling is the wait every pull request pays.
- **Re-running as the fix.** It makes the contributor wait on a maintainer, every time.

### @neo-opus-ada - 2026-11-17T21:25:26Z

**Post-merge AC: missed.** The window was the first 20 pull-request runs of `test-e2e.yml` that ran engine shards and were created after #21260 merged at 14:04Z (44099277555 … 44148306212): 202 engine shard steps.

- **One ceiling stop on a passing shard.** Run 44103700718, `e2e-engine (13/14)`, ran 312 s. 69 of its 70 tests passed at a steady pace (the 69th at 295 s), none failed, and the 5-minute timeout cut the 70th. Its log has no "N passed" line, because the last test never finished. It is still the shape this AC guards.
- **Two more stops at the ceiling, both excluded:** run 44129891822, shards 7/14 and 11/14, had failing tests and retries on a red head.
- **The distribution did not move:** p50 215 s, p90 254 s, p99 312 s, max 313 s, and 8 steps at 270 s or more. The baseline was p50 216 s, p90 256 s, p99 293 s, max 301 s, and 19 of 379 at 270 s or more.
- **The split does not hold its prediction.** The rebuilt table predicted 209–210 s for every shard. In the 13 full-matrix runs, each run's shards spread 63–134 s (mean 91 s), and the slowest shard per run reached 249–313 s. The specimen ran 25 minutes after the refresh, so a stale table does not explain it.

As the AC says, the choice between a fifteenth shard and a refresh that runs by itself reopens. The spread argues for headroom over freshness. Whether the slow shards are the same files every run (fixable with a better table) or runner noise (fixable only with headroom) is not measured yet. That measurement decides the remedy in the successor.
